title: Acute Orthoplastic Care for Complex Open Extremity Fractures in Germany: A Mixed-Methods Study Analyzing Existing Processes
summary: Treating severe, open bone fractures of the arms and legs often requires close cooperation between several medical specialists, for example trauma surgeons and plastic surgeons. So far, little is known about how this cooperation is actually organized in German hospitals and where difficulties arise. In this study, doctors and other healthcare professionals involved in treating these injuries are asked to take part in personal interviews and complete an online questionnaire. The aim is to find out how care is currently organized, what challenges exist, and how it could be improved.
conditions: Complex, open, extremity fractures and severe extremity injuries requiring interdisciplinary orthoplastic care (orthopedic/trauma surgery and plastic surgery). The study does not examine the injuries themselves, but rather the care structures and processes from the perspective of the treating healthcare professionals.

interventions.name: Non-interventional, prospective, web-based mixed-methods study comprising qualitative interviews and an additional cross-sectional survey. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Professional experience or current involvement in the care of severe or complex extremity injuries; working in a medical, therapeutic, or care-related profession (e.g., physicians at various training levels from orthopedic/trauma surgery, plastic surgery, hand surgery, microsurgery, vascular surgery, microbiology/infectious disease, and potentially other professional groups such as orthotics/prosthetics, physiotherapy, or occupational therapy); sufficient German language skills to understand the study information, questionnaire, or interview; provision of informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals under 18 years of age; individuals lacking capacity to consent; individuals without professional experience or relevance to the care of complex extremity injuries; individuals with insufficient German language skills; individuals who do not provide consent to participate or who withdraw consent during the study; patients.
